questions.q: What did physicians discover during autopsies in the sixteenth century that challenged Galen's theory?
a: No black bile was found in cancer patients
Cancer cells were visible to the naked eye
Tumors contained parasitic worms
Black bile was present in all organs
questions.why: Lesson on understanding of cancer: autopsies revealed no black bile in patients.

questions.q: Until 1850, what were people believed to cause tumors?
a: Poisonous vapors and worms
Black bile and poor diet
Inherited genes and radiation
Chemicals and hormonal imbalances
questions.why: Lesson on understanding of cancer: miasmas and worms were the accepted explanation until 1850.

questions.q: What did Percival Pott discover about the cause of scrotal cancer in chimney sweepers?
a: Soot accumulating on their scrotum caused the cancer
A viral infection spread among the boys
A genetic mutation passed from their fathers
Exposure to radiation from the chimneys
questions.why: Lesson on risk factors: Pott linked soot on the scrotum to scrotal cancer in chimney sweepers.

questions.q: How do mutagens cause cancer according to the text?
a: They alter genes affecting cell growth, self-repair, or self-destruction
They directly kill healthy cells in the body
They block the immune system from detecting tumors
They increase the rate of cell division in blood
questions.why: Lesson on risk factors: mutagens alter genes to cause problems in growth, repair, or destruction.

questions.q: Why is surgery limited as a cancer treatment?
a: It cannot remove blood cancers and is ineffective if cells have spread
It causes more DNA damage than chemotherapy
It only works on cancers caused by radiation
It is too expensive for most patients
questions.why: Lesson on treatment: surgery cannot address blood cancers or metastasized cells.
